propositions: When multiple bundle objects exist for a single ref in S3, git ls-remote returns ambiguous SHAs and fresh clones fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', making the store unclonable.

git-remote-s3's upstream Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocking input() calls) and discards non-chosen heads to orphan refs, causing permanent loss of events unique to those heads in an append-only event log.

A non-interactive, lossless heal must detect the multi-bundle state (via 'multiple bundles exists on server' or 'multiple updates for ref' stderr signatures), acquire the helper's per-ref lock to serialize repairs, fetch all divergent heads, perform iterated 2-parent git merges (never octopus or merge=union), write the merged tip as a new bundle before deleting originals, and delete the original bundles only after the merged bundle is durable.

The merge algorithm must follow rebar's existing sync.reconverge semantics (2-parent merges with --allow-unrelated-histories for unrelated heads, content-conflict aborts, no new parameters) and apply the same .gitattributes merge=ours rule for .bridge_state/* that sync already applies.

The heal must maintain a crash-safe invariant: at least one bundle carrying the full merged history must exist remotely at every crash point (merged bundle written before any delete, merged bundle never deleted), so mid-delete crashes recover by re-healing to a single lossless bundle on the next push.
